clue.text: Not work hard for one's daily bread

definitions.meaning: a baked lump of bread, the staple meant by 'daily bread'

explanation.surface: Someone shirking while still expecting to be fed.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to avoid effort, and a baked lump of bread is the proverbial daily staple.

clue.text: One skilled at design makes countries skip about

parts.note: countries are lands
to caper is to skip about playfully

explanation.surface: A designer whose plans make whole nations hop around.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden designer lays out grounds, a job of skilled design.

clue.text: Wax-like substance produced by Mr Big-ears

indicators.note: the letters of the nickname are worked up into something new, as a product is made from raw material

explanation.surface: A waxy stuff apparently made by a man with large ears.
explanation.definitionFit: This waxy secretion from sperm whales is prized in perfumery.

clue.text: Tattles about most of the proclamation, but not the subjects

indicators.note: the chattering word goes around the shortened decree, enclosing it

parts.note: to tattle is to prate, chatter idly

indicators.note: only most of the decree is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a proclamation is an edict

explanation.surface: Gossips chatter over a decree but leave the people it concerns out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' and 'most of' do the work. The definition is grammatical: a sentence divides into its subject and the statement made about it.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a sentence's parts that are not its subjects are its predicates, the statements made about them.

clue.text: In a grand manner but in fact without gravity

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside: the word for 'in fact' sits outside the letter for gravity

parts.note: 'in fact' means really
g is the physics symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: Something done grandly yet, oddly, weightlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, so REALLY goes around G.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting like a monarch means acting with royal grandeur.

clue.text: Dead and tattered but pulled along

parts.note: tattered clothes are ragged

explanation.surface: A lifeless, torn body hauled along the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Hauled along means drawn by force across a surface.

clue.text: Pieces of drill for shopwalkers?

parts.note: parade-ground manoeuvres reversing direction, whimsically read as the marching done behind shop counters by store supervisors

explanation.surface: Military drill applied to department-store floor staff.
explanation.walkthrough: A shopwalker was a supervisor patrolling a British department store's floor, so the word splits into the shop counter plus marching.
explanation.definitionFit: These are drill movements in which a column reverses its direction of march.

clue.text: Atlas has it in brown

indicators.note: the pronoun is placed inside the colour word

parts.note: tan is a light brown

explanation.surface: A map book that happens to contain something brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Atlas' looks like a book of maps; here it is the giant of Greek myth who held up the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlas was one of the giant deities of Greek myth who warred with the Olympians.

clue.text: Earth discovers message about the Dalek's leader

indicators.note: the distress call wraps around the initial letter

parts.note: SOS is the distress message

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Planet Earth finds a distress call about the Doctor Who villain's chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the D from 'leader' of 'Dalek's' inside SOS. Daleks are the robotic villains of the BBC series Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: Clods of turf are pieces of earth cut with the grass.

clue.text: Transmigration starting with me and the s short-term workers

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Transmigration starting with me and the s short-term workers', is garbled after 'the': ME + TEMPS leaves YCHOSIS unaccounted for, and no search gives the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Transmigration starting with me and the s short-term workers

clue.text: Coin which is not base

definitions.meaning: an old English gold coin of the fourteenth to sixteenth centuries

explanation.surface: A coin of pure metal rather than a counterfeit.
explanation.definitionFit: The old English gold piece bore this name, and honourable people are the opposite of base ones.

clue.text: Qualified, being changed step by step

explanation.surface: Someone who has passed their exams after slow, steady progress.
explanation.definitionFit: A student who finished a degree has passed out, and a scale marked in stages is evenly stepped.

clue.text: It brightens the way when there is a different letter in view

definitions.text: It brightens the way when there is a different letter in view

parts.words: It brightens the way when there is a different letter in view
parts.note: lamps illuminating a road at night, with a tease that swapping one letter turns the lamps' glow into something seen

explanation.surface: A riddle about lighting a road and spotting a changed letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half plays on changing L to S, which turns the glow into a sighting, that is, something in view.
explanation.definitionFit: Public lamps along a road brighten the way for walkers and drivers at night.

clue.text: Made unproductive although I tried less irregularly

indicators.note: the letters are set out in no regular order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something rendered barren even though less effort went into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendering an organism barren, or land infertile, makes it unable to reproduce or yield.

clue.text: A prize for degeneration

parts.note: a trophy is a prize such as a cup

explanation.surface: An award handed out for decline, like a booby prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasting away of a body part through disuse is degeneration.

clue.text: The German departed for the river

parts.note: der is a German word for the
departed means went

explanation.surface: A German man left for the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derwent is the name of several English rivers, such as the one through the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Several English waterways bear this name, notably in Cumbria, Derbyshire and Yorkshire.

clue.text: Surprise for one who raises lid?

definitions.meaning: literally something that opens an eyelid

explanation.surface: A shock for someone lifting a lid, perhaps of a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation startles, and the 'lid' of the second reading is an eyelid being opened.

clue.text: Tried with strange sad eyes

indicators.note: the letters are made strange, put into an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: Someone attempted something while looking oddly sorrowful.
explanation.definitionFit: To attempt something is to make an essay at it, an old sense of the verb.

clue.text: Among a hundred Germans this is one who will get to the bottom of things

definitions.text: this is one who will get to the bottom of things

indicators.note: the letters sit among the words, running across 'hundred' and 'Germans'

explanation.surface: A detective found among a crowd of German people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Among' picks out letters spanning hunDRED GERmans. 'Get to the bottom of things' sounds like detection but means scraping a riverbed.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat or machine that scoops mud from the bed of a river literally reaches the bottom.

clue.text: Universal in a mother or lover

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the word for mother

parts.note: mater is Latin for mother, old British schoolboy slang
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A woman who is both a mother and someone's sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts U inside MATER, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-professional pursues something for love of it, from Latin amator, a lover.

clue.text: A treat I change for a song

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Exchanging a treat for a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A short operatic air is a small aria, a kind of song.

clue.text: Church leader's given Andrews science in virtuous address to a friend

parts.note: Archie Andrews was the ventriloquist's dummy in the 1950s BBC radio show Educating Archie

indicators.note: the abbreviation is set inside the run of letters for virtuous and the greeting

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, virtuous
'O pal' is a vocative greeting to a friend
Sc is an abbreviation for science, as in BSc

explanation.surface: An archbishop is joined by a man named Andrews talking science in a pious greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does the inserting. Archie Andrews was a famous British radio ventriloquist's dummy of the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means belonging to an archbishop, the most senior bishop of a province.

clue.text: A woman enters right and left of part of body

indicators.note: the woman's name goes into the gap between the two side letters

parts.note: Ena is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman comes in from stage right and leaves stage left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' puts ENA between R and L.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the kidneys, an organ of the body.

clue.text: A fool loses a page for a friend

indicators.note: one letter is lost from the word for fool

parts.note: a chump is a fool
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: An idiot who drops a page in exchange for a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pal is an informal word for a friend.

clue.text: Hid things wrongly, showing wisdom after the event

indicators.note: the letters are arranged wrongly, so they must be reordered

explanation.surface: Someone who hid things badly later realises the mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Understanding a situation only once it has happened is the classic look back.

clue.text: Birds are almost sufficient for a man

indicators.note: not quite the whole name, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: Ernest is a man's name

explanation.surface: Birds that are nearly good enough for a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts ERNEST to ERNES. 'Sufficient for' is padding linking the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea eagles are birds of prey known in crosswords by this old name.

clue.text: A philosopher with a group of pupils providing energy for the grind

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was an English philosopher
a stream is a group of pupils of similar ability in a British school

explanation.surface: A thinker and a class of students fuelling a hard slog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The grind' sounds like study but is the grinding of corn.
explanation.definitionFit: A current of water channelled to turn a wheel powers a corn-grinding works.

clue.text: Brought up as a bloody revolutionary

parts.note: b is a polite abbreviation for the swear word bloody
a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: Raised as a violent radical.
explanation.definitionFit: Children who were raised were reared, the past tense of the breeding verb.
